content.content:
Scrolling this is messy. Better to just recall known construction periods.

- Great Wall: initial walls 7th–4th century BC; major building under Qin (221–206 BC) connecting; most extant sections from Ming dynasty (1368–1644), especially 14th–17th centuries. So answer: built over centuries, main construction 7th century BC to 16th century AD.

- Petra: capital of Nabataean Kingdom, carved in 1st century BC, major construction 312 BC? Actually city flourished 4th century BC onward; major building 1st century BC to 1st century AD.

- Christ the Redeemer: Rio de Janeiro statue built 1922-1931.

- Machu Picchu: Inca citadel built c. 1450, abandoned 1572.

- Chichen Itza: Mayan city, major construction between 9th–12th centuries AD (approx 600–1200 AD). The Pyramid of Kukulcán built 12th century.

- Roman Colosseum: Construction 72–80 AD.

- Taj Mahal: Built 1632–1653 AD.

The Taj Mahal was designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983 for being "the jewel of Muslim art in India and one of the universally admired masterpieces of the world's heritage". It is regarded by many as the best example of Mughal architecture and a symbol of India's rich history. The Taj Mahal attracts 7-8 million visitors a year,[8] and in 2007 it was declared a winner of the New 7 Wonders of the World (2000–2007) initiative.




## Etymology[edit]


Abdul Hamid Lahori, in his book from 1636 *Padshahnama*, refers to the Taj Mahal as *rauza-i munawwara* (Perso-Arabic: روضه منواره, *rawdah-i munawwarah*), meaning the illumined or illustrious tomb.[9]
The current name for the Taj Mahal is of Urdu origin, and believed to be derived from Arabic and Persian, with the words *tāj mahall* meaning "crown" (*tāj*) "palace" (*mahall*).[10][11][4] The name "Taj" came from the corruption of the second syllable of "Mumtaz".[12][13]

content.content:
Maybe easier to rely on known info: Taj Mahal built 1632–1653 under Shah Jahan.

Christ the Redeemer built 1922–1931.

Great Wall: main sections built 7th century BC to 16th century AD; most visible Ming (1368–1644).

Petra: major building 1st century BC to early 1st century AD.

Machu Picchu: built around 1450, abandoned 1572.

Chichen Itza: major structures built 9th–12th centuries AD (approx 600–1200 AD). The Temple of Kukulcán (El Castillo) built ~12th century.

Roman Colosseum: built 72–80 AD (Vespasian, completed by Titus).

Provide concise answer in table.

Will cite sources? Could use Wikipedia snippets for each. Might need to fetch each. But time limited. Provide answer with approximate years and note ranges.

content:
**New 7 Wonders of the World – approximate dates of construction** | Wonder (modern list) | Main period(s) of construction* | Key points / milestones | |----------------------|--------------------------------|--------------------------| | **Great Wall of China** | **7th century BC – 16th century AD** (most visible sections built **1368‑1644 AD**, Ming dynasty) | • Early walls (state‑period fortifications) began in the 7th century BC.
• The first emperor of a unified China, Qin Shi Huang (221‑206 BC), linked existing walls into a single system.
• The wall was repeatedly rebuilt, expanded and repaired over the next 1 500 years; the massive stone‑brick sections most tourists see today date from the Ming era (mid‑14th to early‑17th century). | | **Petra (Jordan)** | **4th century BC – 1st century AD** (peak building c. 1st century BC) | • The Nabataean kingdom made Petra its capital around the 4th century BC.
• Monumental rock‑cut façades (the Treasury, the Monastery, the Street of Facades) were carved mainly between **100 BC and 1 AD**.
• The city continued to be embellished into the early 2nd century AD before decline after the Roman annexation (106 AD). | | **Christ the Redeemer (Rio de Janeiro, Brazil)** | **1922 – 1931 AD** | • Designed in 1922; construction began in **1931** after a fundraising drive.
• The 30‑metre‑tall Art‑Deco statue was completed and inaugurated on **20 October 1931**. | | **Machu Picchu (Peru)** | **c. 1450 – c. 1530 AD** (abandoned ~1572) | • Built under the Inca emperor **Pachacútec** as a royal estate around **1450**.
• Likely occupied for only a few decades; the Spanish conquest reached the region in the 1530s and the site was abandoned by **c. 1570**. | | **Chichén Itzá (Yucatán, Mexico)** | **c. 600 – 1200 AD** (major Classic‑to‑Post‑Classic phase c. 900‑1100) | • The city grew from a small settlement (≈ 600 AD) into a major Maya‑Toltec centre.
• The iconic **El Castillo (Pyramid of Kukulcán)** and the Great Ball Court were erected in the **10th‑12th centuries AD**. | | **Roman Colosseum (Rome, Italy)** | **72 – 80 AD** | • Construction started under Emperor **Vespasian** in **72 AD**.
• Completed by his son **Titus** in **80 AD** (the arena was inaugurated with games).
• Minor finishing work continued under Emperor Domitian (81‑96 AD). | | **Taj Mahal (Agra, India)** | **1632 – 1653 AD** | • Commissioned by Emperor **Shah Jahan** in **1632** as a mausoleum for his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
• Main marble structure was essentially finished by **1653**; later additions (garden, out‑buildings) continued into the 1660s. | \*The dates given are the **principal building phases** that gave each monument the form we recognise today. All of the sites, except the modern Christ the Redeemer, are the result of centuries‑long development, reconstruction, or expansion; the ranges therefore reflect the longest periods of active construction rather than a single, continuous project.
